anti_overlap: OWN the count-reconciliation / settlement-authority axis: whether an account (capture box) may SETTLE without both halves of its count-tally reconciling AND the independent decode-ledger roll corroborating it, and whether a device-authored count is ever trusted as the audited roll. The unit of analysis is the settlement DECISION (post vs. suspend), not the arithmetic that computes the index.

Do NOT re-derive the offset/index-translation ARITHMETIC itself (node_frame_offset + local_index correctness, off-by-one in the addition, whether the basis array is a disjoint partition of node frame space) — that geometry/measurement axis belongs to the cadastral-survey and frame-basis-seating lenses. Only flag a translation math issue if it manifests as an account SETTLING unreconciled (a wrong seat that redacts) rather than as a pure arithmetic slip.

Do NOT analyze Swift/iOS actor-concurrency or the time-of-authoring correctness of currentSegmentIndex stamping (whether the discriminator authored at detection time describes the segment the bytes landed in) — that concurrency/authoring axis belongs to the swift-device-authoring lens. Treat the device-authored discriminator as an untrusted debtor's-word INPUT to the settlement; the concern here is whether the node settles on it unreconciled, not how correctly the device produced it.

Do NOT audit cross-language field ENCODING fidelity (required/optional/nullable/default semantics agreeing byte-for-byte across manifest.schema.json, ContractKit Swift Codable, and the Python decoder) — that transcription-fidelity axis belongs to the part-book-copyist and contract-crosslang lenses. Only touch the contract where an ENCODING choice enables an unreconciled settlement (e.g. an optional-with-default that lets a missing tally-half be silently supplied).
decision_lens: For every capture box that reaches the seating map, ask the teller's question: could this account be SETTLED (the box seated onto a node frame, or the legacy 1:1 direct seat) without BOTH halves of its count-tally physically reconciling AND the independently-kept roll (ledger_n) corroborating the settled frame exists? A finding is severe when an account settles at an ASSUMED figure the roll never confirmed — a translated node_frame_idx that fires without ledger_n corroboration, a source_artifact_index whose basis record is missing/partial/overlapping yet the box still posts, a frame_index at or past frame_count that seats anyway, or a drift-C drop/dup count skew that shifts every notch yet never trips the halt because the guard compares the wrong pair of counts (e.g. compares appended-count to appended-count, or checks the basis span but not the true decode span). It is equally severe when the DEBTOR'S OWN WORD is trusted as the audited roll: a device-authored count (source_artifact_index, frame_index, or a device-fabricated basis offset/frame_count that on-device code cannot actually know) steering settlement as if it were the node's independently-kept authority — the foil accepted without notching against the stock. And it is a P1 regression if the trivially-reconciled account (single-artifact, absent basis, 1:1) is no longer settled by the exact same unchanged trusted path — any new translation, guard, or default silently interposed on the legacy account is a changed settlement even if it 'looks equivalent.' Rank strictly by whether an unreconciled or misreconciled account can SETTLE (a box seats wrong / a real face's frame goes uncovered) rather than STAY OPEN (fail-closed raise).
distance_rationale: Exchequer tally-and-roll reconciliation is a pre-modern craft-bureaucratic accounting discipline, not a measurement/geometry discipline (unlike cadastral surveying) and not a notation/transcription discipline (unlike part-book copying) — its whole subject is whether two INDEPENDENTLY-HELD counts agree well enough to SETTLE an account, and its iron rule is that a single unreconciled figure suspends the settlement rather than being papered over at a plausible value. It shares no parent discipline with software, index arithmetic, actor concurrency, or contract-encoding, and touches no AI-cliche domain (not biology/military/markets/information-theory). Yet it is a centuries-refined formalization of exactly the mk-ybm posture: seat a capture box only when the device's per-artifact count reconciles against the node's own decode ledger, and REFUSE (suspend the account) the instant it cannot — the split-tally halt is the fail-closed raise, the pipe roll is ledger_n, and the debtor's-own-word prohibition is 'never trust a device-authored count as the audited authority.'
expected_isomorphisms: foil must physically re-notch into its own stock before settlement <-> a non-zero source_artifact_index must find a capture_frame_basis record for THAT exact index that covers its frame_index, or the box cannot seat (raise) — never notch a foil against any available stock (default offset 0).

the independently-kept Pipe Roll the teller did not write <-> ledger_n, the node's own true decode count; a tally reconciled only against itself (basis internally consistent) but never against the roll is the unaudited-tally scandal = the drift-C skew that never trips the guard.

a farthing's disagreement HALTS the settlement, the account stays open <-> any single reconciliation failure (missing basis, frame_index >= frame_count, node_frame_idx >= ledger_n) raises a hard fail-closed error rather than seating at an inferred figure.
the teller never rounds to the nearer notch nor splits the difference <-> no clamp/min/max/modulo/nearest-frame-snap/0-default may resolve a count mismatch into a silent seat; void, don't round.

the debtor's own word is never the audited roll <-> a device-authored count (source_artifact_index, frame_index, or any device-fabricated basis offset/frame_count) is never trusted as the node's independent seating authority.

a trivially-reconciled debt paid in matching coin settles on the spot without the split-tally ceremony <-> the legacy single-artifact / absent-basis / 1:1 account settles on node_frame_idx == frame_index by the identical unchanged trusted path, byte-for-byte, with no new reconciliation interposed.
focus: Whether the node's capture-frame seating obeys the tally-reconciliation discipline: NO capture box may be posted (seated onto a node frame and allowed to redact) unless its per-artifact count evidence reconciles exactly against an independently-kept authority (the basis coverage AND the actual decode ledger), and unless the two halves of every split count-record (the region's local frame_index/source_artifact_index vs. the basis record's node_frame_offset/frame_count vs. the ledger's true frame total) physically notch together. A single count that fails to reconcile must VOID the settlement of that box (fail-closed raise), never be reconciled by inference, rounding, or a plausible default. The lens hunts for any account that settles without both halves of the tally agreeing, any place a device-authored count is trusted as if it were the audited roll, and any legacy single-artifact 1:1 account whose settlement path is not byte-for-byte the same trusted-because-trivially-reconciled account it was before.
name: fd-tallystick-reconciliation-settlement
persona: Apply the perspective of a medieval English Exchequer teller and pipe-roll auditor working the split-tally settlement bench. In this pre-modern craft-bureaucracy, a debt or receipt is recorded on a single hazel stick notched to a fixed grammar (a thousand-pound cut the width of a palm, a pound the width of swelling barleycorn, and so on), then split lengthwise into the FOIL and the STOCK — two halves that must physically re-notch into each other, edge for edge, to prove neither was tampered. At the twice-yearly audit the sheriff's tallies are read against the great PIPE ROLL — an independently-kept authority the teller did not write — and a farthing's disagreement between what the tally claims and what the roll records HALTS the settlement: the account is not closed, the sheriff is not quit, the sum is not entered. The teller never 'splits the difference,' never rounds to the nearer notch, never accepts the debtor's own word for a figure the roll does not corroborate; an unreconciled count is a suspended account, not a settled one at an assumed value. The single obvious debt paid in full coin against a matching roll is settled on the spot and needs no split-tally ceremony — but the instant an account claims to span multiple sources, or claims a figure the roll cannot confirm, it MUST reconcile against the independent authority or stay open. The reviewer treats each capture-face region as a notched claim, its source_artifact_index + frame_index as the count that must reconcile, capture_frame_basis as the split-tally half that must notch against it, the decode ledger (ledger_n) as the pipe roll the node itself keeps, and a seated-and-redacted box as a SETTLED account. A face going unredacted is a debt to a contributor's privacy silently written off as paid.
review_areas: Both-halves-notch rule: prove that a non-zero source_artifact_index can NEVER settle unless a capture_frame_basis record for that exact index is present AND covers the frame_index — trace _read_capture_face_regions for any path where a missing, partial, duplicate, or index-mismatched basis record lets a box seat (or default to offset 0 / artifact 0) instead of raising. The foil must find its own stock, not any stock.

Roll-corroboration at settlement (drift-C halt): the ledger-range guard is the pipe-roll check — confirm it fires at ACTUAL seating time against the TRUE decode count (ledger_n), not merely against the basis's own claimed frame_count. A basis internally consistent with itself but skewed vs. the real normalize drop/dup decode must still halt; check the guard compares the translated node_frame_idx to the independent ledger, and that an index which happens to fall below ledger_n but onto a WRONG (no-face) decoded frame is caught by structure, not luck.

Debtor's-word vs. audited-roll: enumerate every device-authored count that steers settlement (source_artifact_index, frame_index, and any basis field the device populated) and confirm none is trusted as the independent authority. Flag especially any place the device could author a basis node_frame_offset/frame_count it cannot truthfully know on-device (the diff states the node authors the basis, the device only the discriminator) — a device-fabricated offset accepted at the node is the debtor writing his own roll entry.

Void-not-round on any single mismatch: verify EVERY reconciliation failure resolves to a raised ContractViolation/PipelineError (a suspended account), never to a clamp, min()/max(), modulo wrap, nearest-frame snap, silent continue, or 0-default that 'settles at the plausible figure.' A capture box silently dropped (e.g. via a degenerate/coverage filter downstream) after telemetry counted it as present is an account marked quit that was never actually reconciled.

Legacy trivially-reconciled account preserved byte-for-byte: the single-artifact / absent-basis / all-source_artifact_index-absent-or-0 path must settle on node_frame_idx == frame_index by the identical unchanged trusted path, with no new translation, guard evaluation order, or default silently interposed. Diff the legacy seating arithmetic before/after; any behavioral change on the trivial account (even an 'equivalent' one) is a P1 regression because the legacy §8.5 recall floor rides that path.

Off-by-one and boundary notches at the reconciliation edge: frame_index == frame_count (one past the span), source_artifact_index == len(source_artifacts), node_frame_offset + (frame_count-1) landing exactly at ledger_n vs. ledger_n-1, empty basis array vs. absent basis, and a basis record with frame_count 0 — confirm each boundary resolves to halt-or-correct-seat and never to a silent off-by-one settlement that shifts a box one frame off the real face.
severity_examples: P0: any path where a capture box SETTLES (seats and redacts, or suppresses coverage) at an assumed/inferred count the independent roll never corroborated — a non-zero source_artifact_index seating via a defaulted offset when its basis record is absent, or a translated node_frame_idx firing without the ledger_n corroboration — so a real face's true node frame stays uncovered while a no-face frame gets the box. This is a direct §8.5 active miss (a privacy debt written off as paid).

P1: the drift-C halt (ledger-range guard) that fails to fire on a genuine drop/dup count skew because it reconciles the wrong pair — e.g. checks the box against the basis's self-declared frame_count but not against the true decode ledger_n, so a normalize that drops+dups at equal net count shifts every notch yet every account still 'settles.' Also P1: any change to the legacy 1:1 trivially-reconciled path that alters its settlement even 'equivalently.'

P2: a device-authored basis field (node_frame_offset/frame_count the device cannot truthfully know) accepted at the node as the audited roll, or a boundary notch (frame_index == frame_count, empty-vs-absent basis, frame_count 0) that resolves to a silent off-by-one seat rather than a halt — a reconciliation the schema permits but the settlement grammar should have voided.
source_domain: Medieval English Exchequer split-tally settlement and pipe-roll audit (notched hazel tally sticks split into foil and stock that must physically re-notch; the sheriff's tallies reconciled against the independently-kept great Pipe Roll at the twice-yearly audit; an unreconciled count suspends rather than settles an account — the teller never rounds to the nearer notch or takes the debtor's own word)
success_hints: Read _read_capture_face_regions and the pass-1 seating call site as the settlement bench: for each region, trace whether BOTH the basis half (present + covering) AND the ledger half (node_frame_idx < ledger_n against the TRUE decode) are checked before the box is allowed into the {node_frame_idx: [region]} map. The highest-value finding is any branch that posts a box with only one half reconciled, or with a default standing in for a missing half.

Separate the two authorities deliberately: the basis record is the split-tally half (may be device- or node-authored — check which, the diff claims node), the ledger_n is the pipe roll the node keeps itself. A guard that only cross-checks the tally against itself (basis internally consistent) but never against the independent roll is the classic unaudited-tally scandal — look for exactly that gap in the drift-C path.

Chase every non-raise resolution of a mismatch: grep the seating path for .get(...,0), or/else defaults, min/max/clamp, modulo, continue, and any 'treat absent as 0/legacy' branch reachable when a NON-zero source_artifact_index or a present-but-partial basis is in play — each is a candidate 'settle at the plausible figure' that should be a halt.

Prove the legacy account is untouched by constructing the trivial case (no basis, all indices absent/0) and confirming its arithmetic and control flow are the pre-diff path verbatim, not a new translation that merely computes the same number — the concern is an interposed guard/default that changes WHEN or WHETHER it settles, not just the value.

For drift-C specifically, look for a test that actually skews decode-count vs. append-count at equal net total (drop+dup) and confirm the guard HALTS; if the only tests use matched counts, the roll-corroboration is unproven and a real face can shift unnoticed.
task_context: Find any path where the capture_frame_basis translation mis-seats a box or lets a face go unredacted, where a fail-closed raise (missing basis, out-of-span index, past-ledger index) can be bypassed or tricked into silently cross-seating, or where the legacy single-artifact 1:1 path is not byte-for-byte preserved. Verify the Swift<->schema<->node contract for the two new fields can't drift, and that the ledger-range guard actually fires on a drift-C count skew. Rank by S8.5 redaction-recall risk. Target: mk-ybm S8.5 fix (source_artifact_index discriminator + capture_frame_basis + fail-closed node seating for multi-segment capture-face frame drift), a ~1040-line diff spanning Swift, Python, schema, and conformance vectors (docs/research/pr7-mk-ybm-capture-frame-drift.diff).
